subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost pressure
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara@finbot.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost pressure

Sara — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please correct anything I’ve misunderstood.

Key pain points
- Unit economics: current per-query cost is ~ $0.12 at 3B model scale and is unsustainable as you scale to full production (expected 5x growth next 12 months).
- Latency sensitivity: customer-facing chat requires p99 < 250ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Capacity predictability: spikes from batch imports and peak usage make costs and throttling a big risk.

Current stack
- Inference: hybrid — some on-prem NVIDIA A100 for heavy workloads, parts on managed GPUs in GCP (spot instances).
- Serving: custom Flask front-end + basic batching on the client side; no centralized KV prefix caching today.

Success criteria for pilot
- Reduce per-inference spend by at least 3x for your 90th-percentile workload while keeping p99 latency under 250ms.
- Demonstrate batching/caching flow with one of your production prompts to show unit-cost improvement.
- Prove safe quantization path (INT8/4) without >2% drop in classification/regression quality on your eval set.

Open questions / your asks
- Can you share a 24–72 hour sample of request traffic (timestamps + token counts + QPS)?
- Any absolute blockers for model quantization (regulatory, reproducibility, or accuracy thresholds)?
- Procurement timeline (budget window and decision maker contacts).

Next steps
1) Tech deep-dive with Ben (solutions engineer) — 60m to review traffic profile and batching architecture. Suggested slots: Tue 3/17 10am PT or Wed 3/18 9am PT.
2) You share a sanitized 24–72h sample traffic dump (S3 link or CSV).
3) Redwood provides a tailored 4-week pilot plan and a cost-savings estimate (attached).

Attachments: redwood-inference-pilot-plan.pdf (pilot scope & success metrics), SLA-appendix.docx (template).

If this looks right I’ll book the technical call and send a short intake form for the traffic sample.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference | High-performance, predictable LLM inference

From: Sara Kim <sara@finbot.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finbot.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost pressure

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications:

- The $0.12/req is our current blended cost (we calculate tokens differently across teams), and the 5x growth projection is correct — peak QPS can be 4–5x baseline during campaigns.
- Latency target: we can be flexible on long-form generation, but customer chat must stay under p99 250ms for short prompts.
- Quantization: our ML org is open to INT8; INT4 would require a quality validation run. Regulatory is not a blocker, but model drift concerns mean we need a reproducible eval.

We can provide a sanitized CSV of request timestamps + token_in + token_out + endpoint tag. I’ll loop in procurement separately for any contract/PO questions (they’re on copy).

Regarding timeline — we’re looking to have a pilot contract executed in the next 6–8 weeks. If Redwood can show a clear cost model and a short pilot scope, we have internal buy-in to move quickly.

Happy to take Ben’s call on Tue 3/17 10am PT.

— Sara
Sara Kim
Head of ML, FinBot
sara@finbot.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara@finbot.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost pressure

Perfect — I’ve booked Tue 3/17 10:00am PT for the technical deep-dive with Ben. Calendar invite sent.

Next immediate items from our side:
- Ben will build an initial cost model for your traffic shape once we receive the sample CSV (we’ll share assumptions).
- I’m attaching a short one-page pilot plan and SLA appendix — it’s intentionally lightweight to speed procurement review.
- We’ll include an optional quantization validation step in the pilot (INT8 baseline + INT4 experiment) and surface a quality gating process tied to your eval set.

Ben — can you prepare an initial throughput/batching sketch and a list of exact fields we need in the CSV? Example: timestamp, endpoint, request_tokens, response_tokens, user_id_hash (or anon id).

Sara — can you confirm who on your side will deliver the traffic sample and whether S3 or Drive is preferred?

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Marissa

Attachments: redwood-inference-pilot-plan.pdf, SLA-appendix.docx
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/FINBOT-246

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sara Kim <sara@finbot.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost pressure

Quick note from engineering side ahead of tomorrow’s call:

I’ll bring an initial cost model and a couple of batching strategies to test (dynamic batching vs fixed-window). For the CSV, the exact minimal fields we need: timestamp (ISO), endpoint_tag, request_tokens, response_tokens, and a boolean field for high-priority (true/false). If you can include CPU/GPU utilization samples for any on-prem runs that would help for baseline comparison.

Also — if you can share a few representative prompts (anonymized) that would let us run a small quality pass on INT8 quantization before we run the pilot. We won’t need raw PII.

See you on the call.

— Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
